relevance_note: Systematic review with a per-patient table of PAMI patients carrying PSTPIP1 variants: 'we included 25 relevant articles that described 43 patients with PAMI syndrome'.
method_note: Systematic review of 43 PAMI patients (PSTPIP1 E250K or E257K) summarised in Table 1, one row per patient; no supplementary file text was available. A Python script in my scratch directory transcribed Table 1 cells and built the rows from my per-cell reading; I checked its output against the table. Labels: Table 1 has a bare-number 'N°' column, so labels are 'Table 1 #<n>'. The number 14 is printed twice (Mendonca et al. row and the following Laberko et al. row; the numbering then continues at 16, so no #15 exists); these are labelled 'Table 1 #14 (row 14)' and 'Table 1 #14 (row 15)'. The Laberko row's Author cell is split by a line break in the Markdown; its spans include that line break. The text's 'patient N° 8, Table 1' (lupus-like phenotype) was mapped to Table 1 #8. Variants: the review gives no per-patient variant; it states 41/43 carried heterozygous E250K and 2/43 E257K without saying which patients, so every patient has a PSTPIP1 variant row with variant_original_string 'not reported' and zygosity 'not reported'. 'Age in Years' column recorded as age at last evaluation/report; it may instead be age at diagnosis (the text says age at diagnosis ranged from 6 months to 56 years, matching this column's range), so treat with caution. Table cells 'No' were read as explicit absence for that column (Fever, Growth Failure, Lymphadenopathy Hepatosplenomegaly, Dermatologic Signs, Osteoarticular Signs); 'No' under Dermatologic Signs excluded pyoderma gangrenosum, acne and hidradenitis but not the composite 'skin or soft-tissue abscesses'; 'No' under Osteoarticular Signs excluded arthritis and osteomyelitis; 'No' under Other Symptoms excluded nothing. 'NA' = not reported. 'Pancytopenia' was taken as anemia and thrombocytopenia observed (neutropenia left not reported); 'Leucopenia' alone did not mark neutropenia. Osteomyelitis not stated as aseptic/sterile (#25, #26, #29, #43) and staph aureus osteomyelitis (#23) left the sterile-osteomyelitis checklist item not reported; arthralgia, elbow pain, polyarthropathy, knee swelling, morning stiffness and dactylitis did not mark arthritis. Elevated inflammatory markers marked observed for all 43 from the group statement 'Systemic inflammation was evidenced in all reported cases' (#3 also individually: 'high inflammatory markers'). Hyperzincemia and hypercalprotectinemia were reported only for 'all tested patients' without naming them, so not reported. Relatives: rows were created for relatives described as having PAMI or carrying the variant: father of #12, mother of #27, son of #28, father of #37 (PAMI) and father of #25 (same mutation, no symptoms). Not merged, but they probably duplicate table rows: father of #12 is likely #11 (same reference [21]), mother of #27 is likely #28 and son of #28 likely #27 (same reference [2]). Relatives with other conditions (arthritis, alopecia areata, psoriatic arthritis, gout, SLE/RA, telomere disorder) and healthy untested parents got no rows. HSCT by Laberko et al. [20] for 'five patients' was not assigned to the four Laberko rows because the paper does not say which patients. Contradictions: Table 1 #14 (row 14) has Fever 'No' but Other Symptoms 'During childhood recurrent fever' (both rows emitted, fever checklist not reported). Table 1 #10 has age of onset '6 years' but age 2.5 (recorded as printed). The text says 41/43 E250K are 'heterozygous' but this was not applied per patient.

disease_label_as_stated.span: ### Table 1: Clinical features of patients with PAMI syndrome.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic: PAMI-specific PSTPIP1 variant (E250K or E257K) required for inclusion; 41 of 43 E250K, 2 of 43 E257K, not assigned per patient
span: Genetic analysis of the PSTPIP1 gene revealed that in a significant majority of cases, 41 out of 43 (95%) exhibited the heterozygous E250K variant. Only two patients in our review had the E257K variant.
Confirmed PAMI syndrome in the presence of one of the PAMI-specific PSTPIP1 gene deleterious variants (E250K or E257K).

span: Genetic analysis of the PSTPIP1 gene revealed that in a significant majority of cases, 41 out of 43 (95%) exhibited the heterozygous E250K variant. Only two patients in our review had the E257K variant.
Confirmed PAMI syndrome in the presence of one of the PAMI-specific PSTPIP1 gene deleterious variants (E250K or E257K).
